features.label: Beaked figure
features.definition: A beaked head on the selected figure; a museum deity name alone is insufficient.

features.label: Arm or wing extends forward
features.definition: A limb projects in front of the selected beaked figure. An arm and a wing remain different anatomical readings.

features.label: Separate rounded form
features.definition: A disc, ring or compact rounded object, excluding an eye, body outline or suspension hole.

features.label: Rounded form at the limb
features.definition: The same beaked figure’s arm or wing reaches to the rounded form. Nearness does not prove a grip or shared meaning.

features.label: Facing beaked figures
features.definition: Two beaked figures face one another within the same scene. Separate objects never create this feature.

events.label: Bird imagery at Göbekli Tepe
events.finding: Several local pillars show birds with varied anatomy.
events.limit: Site context does not directly date a particular carved feature.

events.label: A modified crane wing at Çatalhöyük
events.finding: Cuts on wing bones were interpreted as attachment work; costume use is one proposed explanation.
events.limit: Not a bird-and-disc image or a demonstrated link to Rapa Nui. This broad range dates the mound context, not the individual wing.

events.label: Thoth in several forms
events.finding: The selected museum objects include a beaked human and an ibis beside a feather.
events.limit: Separate objects and widely separated dates. They do not establish an intermediate route.

events.label: A local repertoire at Nimrud
events.finding: Eagle-headed and human-headed figures share the palace’s protective imagery.
events.limit: Related reliefs from one palace are not independent cultural origins.

events.label: Independent evidence of Pacific contact
events.finding: Ancient genomes support pre-European American ancestry in Rapanui.
events.limit: This dates an ancestry event, not these carvings or a connection with Anatolia.

events.label: The moai’s sequence has an endpoint
events.finding: The study uses early photographs alongside surface recording to examine later carving and damage.
events.limit: The ring predates the birdman composition in the study’s reading. The carving episodes still lack precise absolute dates.

events.label: The boulder in an early photograph
events.finding: Routledge’s figure 112 already shows the birdman and identifies the egg.
events.limit: This proves the carving existed by 1914. It does not directly establish the approximate museum date range.

events.label: A recorded local meaning
events.finding: Routledge describes carrying the egg on the upturned hand and records local birdman traditions.
events.limit: A mediated historical account; it cannot supply the unknown meaning of the Neolithic disc.

events.label: The paired scene in another medium
events.finding: The museum identifies two facing tangata manu on a painted Orongo slab.
events.limit: 1974 is a transfer date. No production date is supplied in the inspected record.

hypotheses.title: Local development and recurrence
hypotheses.prediction: Local variants connect the figures to particular practices; broad ingredients recur with different arrangements and meanings.
hypotheses.evidence: Local bird repertoires are documented on both sides. The egg has a Rapanui historical context; the Neolithic disc remains ambiguous.
hypotheses.missing: A fuller regional sequence and a defined comparison collection are still needed. Local context alone does not rule out older inheritance.
hypotheses.next: Acquire further dated Orongo scenes and nearby Anatolian bird compositions, preserving less similar examples.

hypotheses.title: Transmission through intermediates
hypotheses.prediction: Several specific details recur together in a dated sequence, with independent evidence supporting the proposed connections.
hypotheses.evidence: Pacific–American contact has independent support. The selected Egyptian and Assyrian parallels are comparisons, not a demonstrated route from Anatolia.
hypotheses.missing: No connected sequence for this precise motif has been established by this investigation.
hypotheses.next: Search dated intermediates for the whole arrangement, including its unusual differences, and log unsuccessful searches.

hypotheses.title: A much older shared inheritance
hypotheses.prediction: The specific arrangement is attested early enough, persists or transforms through intervening traditions, and comes with evidence beyond generic resemblance.
hypotheses.evidence: The large chronological separation leaves a question, but does not itself supply a line of descent.
hypotheses.missing: Earlier Pacific attestations and a transmission history for the motif have not been established here. This small corpus cannot prove global absence.
hypotheses.next: Specify the expected inherited details and regions before expanding the search. Seek independent chronological and material support.

hypotheses.title: Selection and presentation amplify the match
hypotheses.prediction: Similarity changes with view, cropping, feature definition or the alternatives included.
hypotheses.evidence: The museum queries returned ordinary variants, holes, headdresses and incomplete figures. The three focal objects differ in limb, arrangement and certainty of meaning.
hypotheses.missing: The annotations need independent review; the current set was assembled for exploration and cannot estimate worldwide rarity.
hypotheses.next: Review the reference regions, then freeze a new recognition test using alternate views and close visual alternatives.

findings.title: The arrangement is the sharper question.
findings.text: Pillar 43 and the boulder both place a rounded form at an extended limb of a beaked figure. Their limbs, poses and evidential support for meaning differ.

findings.title: The ring deserves its published alternative.
findings.text: The 2014 study proposes that the moai’s older ring was absorbed into the later birdman scene, perhaps as an egg. Damaged arms make a simple “held / not held” verdict too strong.

findings.title: The historical bridge is still missing.
findings.text: The examples make specific resemblances inspectable. They do not yet supply a dated chain carrying this arrangement between Anatolia and Rapa Nui.
